title: Quadratic-size submodular hypergraph sparsifiers
formal: Does there exist an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that every submodular hypergraph on \(n\geq1\) vertices and every \(0<\varepsilon<1\) admit a reweighted sub-hypergraph with at most \(C n^{2}/\varepsilon^{2}\) hyperedges that simultaneously approximates every cut value within factors \(1-\varepsilon\) and \(1+\varepsilon\)?
why: The question asks whether rich higher-order cut objectives always have representations using quadratically many original terms, independent of their complexity and value ranges. Such a theorem would provide a general compression guarantee across submodular optimization models.
status_note: Conjecture 1.14 is explicit in the 2024 paper. On 13 September 2026 the later-work check verified the statement, but not the proof, of a July theorem restricted to bounded integral functions and the abstract of an August symmetric-function result. Neither states the full conjectured bound for arbitrary splitting functions; status remains source_open.

progress.text: The source proves a general cubic bound in \(n\) and poses Conjecture 1.14 for the quadratic bound.

Theorem 1.5 of the new preprint gives a nearly quadratic bound with inverse-fourth accuracy dependence for bounded integral submodular functions. The general nonnegative case remains outside its stated theorem.
A separate preprint reports linear-size sparsifiers for symmetric submodular sums. Its abstract was checked, but the proof was not independently verified.

importance.reason: A general quadratic compression conjecture for arbitrary submodular cut objectives, including asymmetric and unbounded-range splitting functions.

sentences: A submodular hypergraph assigns each hyperedge a flexible submodular cost for being split by a cut.
A sparsifier retains and reweights hyperedges so that every cut value remains approximately correct.
The conjecture proposes a quadratic-in-vertices size bound with inverse-squared accuracy dependence in the source's size measure.
Preserving exponentially many cuts simultaneously is the main obstacle identified there.
The project seeks a compression theorem extending beyond ordinary all-or-nothing hyperedge cuts to richer models used in optimization and learning.

definitions: A submodular hypergraph \(H=(V,E,(g_e)_{e\in E})\) has a finite vertex set \(V\), \(|V|=n\), a finite set \(E\subseteq2^V\) of hyperedges, and, for each \(e\), a function \(g_e:2^e\to\mathbb R_{\geq0}\) with \(g_e(\varnothing)=0\). Submodularity means \(g_e(A\cup B)+g_e(A\cap B)\leq g_e(A)+g_e(B)\) for every \(A,B\subseteq e\). Neither symmetry under complementation nor monotonicity, bounded positive-value ratios, integral values or bounded hyperedge rank is assumed; in particular \(g_e(e)\) need not vanish. A cut is any \(S\subseteq V\) and its value is \(F_H(S)=\sum_{e\in E}g_e(S\cap e)\). A reweighted sub-hypergraph chooses \(E'\subseteq E\) and one real scalar \(w_e>0\) for each retained edge, giving \(F_{H'}(S)=\sum_{e\in E'}w_e g_e(S\cap e)\). It must satisfy \((1-\varepsilon)F_H(S)\leq F_{H'}(S)\leq(1+\varepsilon)F_H(S)\) for every \(S\subseteq V\), including exact preservation of zero-valued cuts. Size counts retained hyperedges, not total incidences, splitting-function descriptions or bits. This is an existence theorem: no input-oracle representation, construction time, coefficient bit bound or random failure probability is imposed. The constant \(C\) must be independent of every hypergraph parameter and of \(\varepsilon\).

context_blocks.text: Theorem 1.4 of Kenneth and Krauthgamer gives an \(O(n^3/\varepsilon^2)\) reweighted sparsifier for arbitrary nonnegative submodular splitting functions. Their Conjecture 1.14 asks whether the vertex dependence can be reduced to quadratic, while retaining the stated accuracy dependence and the original splitting functions.

A July 2026 preprint proves a \(\widetilde O(n^2/\varepsilon^4)\) bound when all functions take values in a fixed finite integer range. Its Theorem 1.5 and following discussion explicitly leave arbitrary nonnegative submodular functions outside that result.

An August 2026 preprint reports \(O(n/\varepsilon^2)\) sparsifiers for sums of symmetric submodular functions. Symmetry is an additional promise absent here; it does not cover arbitrary directed or asymmetric splitting costs.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of a universal constant and the stated simultaneous reweighted sparsifier bound, or prove its negation. A refutation must rule out every possible universal constant, not just one proposed bound. Bounds with additional logarithmic losses, a worse power of inverse accuracy, restricted splitting functions, or newly invented splitting functions do not establish the conjecture.

notes: Recovered nonnegative submodularity with only the empty-set normalization; did not impose symmetry or zero value on the full hyperedge.
Defined cut values, simultaneous relative approximation, positive per-edge reweighting and hyperedge-count size; no construction-time or bit-complexity claim was added.
Checked the exact July 2026 bounded-range theorem and the August symmetric result, retaining their distinct restrictions and accuracy dependence.
